Definition: from φάρμακον (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician:--sorcerer.
BiblicalUsage: Pharmakeus is a sorcerer, one who deals in drugs and spells, and it appears in the list of those whose part is in the lake of fire. The fearful and unbelieving, the abominable and murderers, the whoremongers and sorcerers and idolaters and liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sorcerer's place in that list is no accident: sorcery promises power and delivers death, and its end is the second death.
